d: Women-only sport and wellness community across BLR, MUM, DEL NCR, HYD, MYQ, MAA. Free events, RSVP required. Occasional mixed-gender editions as 'Sisters and Misters'. Popular 5K Cubbon Park runs.

Bengaluru-based social club for everyday athletes. Weekly community runs and multi-sport meetups. Collaborations with Nike India (RiseIndia), Sisters in Sweat, Bastian Yoga. Also organized India's first tower run at UB City.
1000+ member run club. Morning runs at Cubbon Park and Ecoworld Bellandur. 3K and 5K runs. Post-run coffee culture, wellness pop-ups. Open to all levels.
Beginner-friendly running collective that welcomes all levels to free meetups, usually ending in a relaxed coffee. The whole focus is on making running accessible.

3000+ member Strava-based cycling club, one of Bengaluru's most active. Regular group rides across the city and outskirts.

Long-running Google Groups mailing list-based cycling community. Older-school culture, focused on ride planning and biking conversations. Includes kids' cycling initiatives (GGI - Go Green Initiators).

Bengaluru's largest trekking organisation, running around six treks every weekend. Popular routes include Kodachadri, Kumara Parvatha and Tadiyandamol in Coorg, and it also runs Himalayan expeditions. Fixed-departure paid model with well-organised logistics.
Popular trek and travel organization known for being helpful to newbies. Weekend treks around Karnataka + longer Himalayan trips. Strong community reviews for beginner-friendliness.
3,700+ Instagram community. Weekend treks around Karnataka. Regular event schedule shared on Instagram.

Non-profit outdoor group covering trekking, cycling, biking, rock climbing, wildlife photography, and eco-conservation. Runs treks to Bhimana Kindi and Ramanagara plus Himalayan expeditions. Volunteer-driven.

1,100+ member trekking group co-founded by Deepika Muthusamy and Santosh Kumar Gupta in 2014. Weekend treks and longer expeditions. Strict 'no alcohol, no smoking, no littering' policy. Photography-forward.
Adventure and trekking group for enthusiasts who don't have their own gear. Rents equipment as part of trek packages.

Themed neighbourhood walking tours, from dosa walks and Malleshwaram mornings to colonial crawls. Sits comfortably between movement and food, and works as a slow, unhurried way to cover ground on foot.
Silent reading community that meets in public parks for a shared reading session, followed by bookish conversation. Calm and screen-free, and also active in Mumbai, Pune and Jaipur.
Pay-as-you-like weekend gatherings run by Anne, taking in the Museum of Curiosities, zine making and letter writing. Slow, screen-free and community-first, and good for mental restoration.
Climbing gym + community. 1,900+ Instagram. Regular members' sessions, coaching, and community climbing events. Closed Mondays.
13k+ Instagram community around Bengaluru's first indoor climbing gym (est. 2013). Bouldering, sport climbing, calisthenics, yoga. Regular climbing socials, route-setting workshops, community trips.

Queer and trans folks football group, meeting every Sunday since Jan 2024. Started by a co-founder who wanted a group not composed exclusively of straight men. Open to all queer persons including queer women. Rain or shine.

Volunteer-run non-profit offering a safe, inclusive space for LGBTQIA+ people and allies to play and learn badminton. Meets three days a week, and runs the annual Queer Badminton League during Pride month.
Cricket group for all queer persons except cis-men. Contact through reference only. Small but active, part of Bengaluru's growing queer sports ecosystem.
Safe space for queer, trans, and non-binary folks to learn and celebrate Tango dance. Movement-based community with dance's characteristic warmth.
India's first LGBTQ+ inclusive travel and experience community. Queer-inclusive trips, treks, workshops, and hangouts. End-to-end logistics in inexpensive packages.
Bengaluru's oldest queer support group, running since 1994. Weekly meetings at the Swabhava office cover discussions, film screenings and poetry readings, every Thursday and Sunday.
Peer-to-peer support group for LBT+ persons only (queer and not-cis-men). Non-registered, operating via internet and word of mouth. Democratic, leaderless, inclusive, non-commercial. Since 2009.
Youth-focused (under 30) queer support group and safe space. Since 2011. Frequent meetings and potlucks, often at Cubbon Park. Self-funded.
Queer people and allies meet fortnightly at rotating venues to play board games. Low-stakes and social, and a gentle entry point for introverts and anyone new to the city's queer scene.

Bengaluru chapter of a global community (36,000+ across 45 cities) that brings founders, investors, tech people, and creatives together for weekly easy runs + networking. Pets/family welcome. Coffee-and-conversations format.

Charitable women's community, part of Ladies Circle India. 9,700+ followers. Combines charity work with wellness-adjacent social events, networking, and community-building. Not fitness-primary but a strong women's network.
Neighborhood community for socializing sober in HSR Layout. Regular events focused on connection without alcohol. Wellness angle: mental health, mindful socializing.
Free monthly breakfast lecture series for creative professionals. Global chapter model. RSVP required. Wellness angle: creativity as mental well-being, community around ideas.
Annual festival of queer films from around the world, held at Alliance Française. Art, representation and community celebration in one weekend.
Verified directory of run clubs, marathon training groups, and weekend trail collectives across Bengaluru. RSVP to club runs. Useful cross-reference to discover clubs not listed here.

ad: Gatthalli Rd, Gattahalli, Janatha Colony, Karnataka 560099
d: Four synthetic courts with good cushioning, ample parking and clean washrooms, priced below comparable venues — a player whose son competes nationally rates it in the elite bracket. Nothing is available on rent, so bring your own racket and shuttles. Mosquitoes are a real problem in the evenings.

ad: VPV9+2CR, Kodathi, Kodathi JHC, Karnataka 560035
d: Six cost-effective courts with wooden-plus-synthetic flooring under a head coach who has run the academy for years, with rackets and shoes on rent and good spectator seating. Parking for two and four wheelers, clean changing and rest rooms. It gets hot inside, and no food or drinks are sold on site.

ad: 546, 1st Main Rd, Kothnur, Royal County, 8th Phase, Lal Bahadur Shastri Nagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560083
d: Heated pool with hot-water showers and dedicated slots and trained staff for children with special needs — families travel from other states for the coaching here. Strength and endurance sessions run alongside the swimming. The pool itself is small and 5 ft throughout.
b: Special needs coaching, Kids, Adults learning

ad: Balaji Layout, Chokkanahalli, Sampigehalli Rd, near VIBGYOR School Road, Sampigehalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560064
d: Three wooden indoor courts with excellent lighting and smooth flooring, plus box cricket and football. Rackets, shuttles, shoes, socks, energy drinks and bars all sold on site, so you can turn up in street clothes. Multiple changing rooms. Ventilation could be better.

ad: 224, 1st Main Rd, Kempegowdanagar, Maheswari Nagar, T Dasarahalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560057
d: Three courts at around ₹210 an hour with racket and shoe rental at ₹30, mineral water and washrooms, plus swimming coaching on the same site that reviewers credit with teaching them inside ten days. Friendly owner. Side-on shots catch the lighting awkwardly.
b: Budget play, Swimming lessons, Gear rental

ad: 142/2, near Maramma Temple, Vaderahalli, Vidyaranyapura, Karnataka 560097
d: Newer site combining indoor pickleball, badminton with generous space around the courts, outdoor box cricket on green turf with good bounce, football and a gym. Coaching across cricket, football and badminton. Parking for both two and four wheelers, rates described as nominal.

ad: 117, 1st Cross Rd, IDBI Layout, Kalena Agrahara, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560083
d: Six courts on premium wooden flooring in a large, green, quiet compound — ₹200 an hour at peak and ₹100 from 10 AM to 6 PM, with rackets and shoes from ₹25. Own parking inside the compound, separate changing rooms, bulk-booking discounts direct. Google routing here is unreliable, so allow time.

ad: 735/3/11-12, Bommanahalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560068
d: Five indoor pickleball courts with generous run-off, a raised viewing deck, showers and changing rooms. Paddles on rent and regular sports shoes are fine — no non-marking requirement. Gets hot indoors. Mornings are deserted and staff have been late opening the shutter for early slots.

ad: 10/5, Kembathalli Main Rd, opposite Sree Bayalu Anjaneya Swamy Temple, South Avenue, Gottigere, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560083
d: A 25m temperature-controlled indoor pool across five lanes, 3 ft to 5.5 ft, with water-quality parameters displayed openly — chlorine and TDS posted for anyone to read. Badminton courts, turf, a licensed sports shop and a strong coaching roster alongside. Showers have geysers but hot water is inconsistent, and play-session rules on kickboards have changed without notice.

ad: Swamy Muneshwara Complex, 194/3, Bagalur Main Rd, Munneshwara Block, Kattigenahalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560063
d: Swimming at around ₹200 an hour in a well-kept pool with showers, shelves and clean washrooms, plus badminton, turf, a gym and a food court. Caps and nylon swimwear are compulsory and sold on site. Equipment on rent. Weekend slots book out to midnight, so plan ahead.

ad: 5th A Cross, Laxminarayana Temple Road, Munnekollal, Laxminarayana Layout, Thubarahalli, Marathahalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560037
d: 4.9 across 229 reviews. Nets with a bowling machine in a quiet setting that suits focused practice, and a head coach reviewers repeatedly describe as honest and hands-on in a market they call over-commercialised. Particularly strong on playing spin. Parking on site.
b: Net practice, Kids coaching, Bowling machine

ad: SMVM & BAPU Institution Campus, 8th Main Rd, Judicial Layout 2nd Phase, Jyotipuram, Mallasandra, Karnataka 560109
d: Ten courts — three wooden, seven synthetic — with a balcony for spectators, a judge’s seat, an on-site badminton shop doing gutting, and a food stall. Weekend rates through Playo are better than most courts in the city. Structured 1:1 coaching by age group. Lighting is a touch dimmer than the best nearby venues.

ad: Coco Sports Arena, Bommenahalli Village, near Old School Fitness Gym, Bidarahalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560049
d: Eight new premium courts on wooden base with synthetic matting, easy on the legs over long sessions and well matted throughout. Parking on site plus plenty on the road outside. Still bedding in — no reception desk yet and the court lighting angle catches players’ eyes on some courts.
b: Regular players, Long sessions, New courts

ad: Beerashwara Residential Apartment, 434/1, 3rd B Cross Rd, Gopalappa Layout, NRI Layout, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560016
d: Four courts at very reasonable rates with parking inside the campus, clean restrooms, drinking water and shoes on rent. Walk-ins usually get a court at off-peak. It is an older arena — the flooring and lighting are due an upgrade, space around the courts is tight and ventilation is limited.

ad: Sarjapur–Marathahalli Rd, near Advaith Hyundai Showroom, Sarjapura, Sompura, Bengaluru, Karnataka 562125
d: Badminton, basketball, box cricket, cricket nets, football and skating on one main-road site, with half-hour incremental booking slots — rare and genuinely useful if you want 90 minutes rather than a round two. Good synthetic courts that hold up over long sessions. Football coaching draws criticism as commercially driven, with a ₹2,000 kit requirement.

ad: 126/5, Sulikunte Village, Varthur Hobli, Main Road, Sulikunte Colony, Sarjapur, Karnataka 562125
d: The most complete facility on the shortlist — air-conditioned badminton courts, squash, basketball, football, swimming and a shooting range, with washrooms players describe as five-star. National-level coaches, and the Indian Basketball League has been played here. Closes at 9 PM, earlier than most.

ad: Play Feathers, Venu Gopal Reddy Ln, Doddamane Krishnappa Layout, BTS Layout, Arekere, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560076
d: Four hybrid wooden courts in a newer, clean venue with better lighting than most nearby and ample car and two-wheeler parking. Priced above other courts in the area. Seating is limited, and the shoe policy is strictly enforced — non-marking alone is not enough, so check before you travel.

ad: Neeladri Rd, Bettadasanapura, Vittasandra, Karnataka 560100
d: Ten courts on BWF-standard flooring with shock-absorbing mats, high ceiling clearance, glare-free LEDs and proper ventilation — technically one of the better-specified venues in Electronic City. Coaching for kids and adults, rackets and shoes on rent, separate changing rooms for men and women.

ad: DMM Garden, 1st Main Rd, Vidya Nagar, T Dasarahalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560057
d: Open round the clock with badminton, a cricket turf, table tennis, chess and a swimming pool that a visiting swim instructor rates for water clarity and safety protocols. Zumba runs here too. Court 6 is in poor shape, the changing room is used as storage, and floodlights on the cricket turf need repeated chasing.

ad: Jambusawari Dinne, Royal County, South Avenue, Gottigere, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560083
d: Three premium teakwood courts with distinctive red mats, a balcony overlooking all three, changing rooms and RO water. ₹200 to ₹300 depending on time and day — afternoons are cheapest. Clean and well run, with coaching across levels. Slightly interior but the approach road is good.

ad: Reliable Silver Oak, 33, Main Road, next to Orchids School Road, Haralur, Eastwood Township, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560102
d: Newer arena rated 4.8 across 253 reviews, with a well-drained turf that plays fine straight after rain, cricket nets with a quality bowling machine and side-arm coaching, pickleball and table tennis. A cafe on site does juices and energy drinks. Off the main road, so two-wheeler parking is on site and cars go on the road.

ad: 88/2, behind HP Petrol Bunk, Chaitanya Ananya, Seegehalli, Kadugodi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560115
d: Around seven courts, all recently re-cushioned with rubber underlay, under BWF-certified coaches — and among the cheapest options in Whitefield. Shop on site for shirts, shoes, rackets and bags. Shower and changing facilities, ample car parking. Football, cricket, swimming, tennis and a gym on the same campus.

ad: Survey No. 18, D Cube Sports Club, State Highway 104, Main Road, Sathanur, Bagaluru, Bengaluru, Karnataka 562149
d: Well-kept floodlit turf for 5-a-side and 7-a-side inside a community clubhouse, with rugby and ultimate frisbee also played here — one of very few rugby-capable venues in the city. Restrooms and changing rooms are well maintained and there is a restaurant on site. Kids’ coaching runs at weekends.

ad: Nisarga Orchards, Papareddy Palya, Marilingappa Extension, Nagarbhavi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560072
d: Five wooden courts across two floors with good lighting, plus a temperature-controlled indoor pool at 5 ft that beginners rate for cleanliness and friendly coaching. Table tennis, yoga and carrom too. Weekend badminton is ₹300 an hour. Two-wheeler parking is plentiful; car parking is effectively nil.

ad: Kambipura Rd, Anchepalya, Kambipura, Karnataka 560074
d: Around ₹250 an hour with a flexible owner and a decent regular playing group, and it hosts local tournaments. The main option on this stretch of Mysore Road. Maintenance is the weak point — at least one reviewer rates nearby courts better for less.

ad: 27/1, behind Fullinfaws College, next to Axis Antara, Yelenahalli, Akshayanagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560114
d: Multiple well-kept grounds taking football, box cricket and ultimate frisbee, with seating for parents, drinking water and clean restrooms. A soccer club runs coaching here and reviewers single out the kids’ coach. Direct or Playo booking, open till 11 PM.

ad: Royal Enclave Rd, Sidedahalli, Soundarya Layout, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560073
d: Newer wooden courts with extra space around them so players are not colliding, solid grip that reduces knee strain, glare-free lighting and proper changing rooms. Among the cheapest in the area. A 2026 tournament here drew heavy criticism over shuttle quality, officiating and unawarded medals — fine for play, less so for competition.

ad: Atya Sports, Sy No. 188/4, S Bingipura, Electronic City, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560100
d: Four new premium wooden courts with good lighting and a large parking area. Genuinely remote — the approach road is poor, there are no shops nearby for refreshments, nothing is available on rent, and public transport back is difficult. Come by car with your own gear.

ad: 4G6H+465, Bylakere, Karnataka 560089
d: Indoor stadium with wooden flooring under synthetic mats giving real cushion, accurate markings, correct net height and good ventilation. Owner-run and well kept — regulars rate it among the best courts they have played on. Quiet venue, so few open games are posted on Playo; bring your own group.
b: Groups with own players, Regular play

ad: Pattanagere, 2nd Main Rd, near Rajarajeshwari Temple Road, BHEL Layout, Rajarajeshwari Nagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560098
d: Six courts with quality flooring and coaching that covers technique, fitness and match strategy, plus clean toilets, generous parking and a relaxed policy on footwear. Ventilation is the recurring complaint — one reviewer could not complete a two-hour booking. The seating platform sits slightly above the court edge, so watch the step.

ad: Vyasa International School, Doddabommasandra, North BEL Gate Post, Vidyaranyapura, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560013
d: Well-kept courts inside a school campus with a genuinely calm entrance and surroundings, ventilated with a decent seating area between matches. Around ₹95 per person for 90 minutes via Playo — among the cheapest anywhere on this list. Two-wheeler parking is plentiful; cars are harder. Split hours on weekdays.

ad: 1st Cross Rd, Anemma Green Garden, 1st A Cross Rd, Akshaya Nagar 1st Block, Ramamurthy Nagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560016
d: Five wooden and synthetic courts with adequate lighting, phone shelves and charging points courtside, and half-hour booking increments through Playo. A licensed sports shop and gutting service on site. Rates from around ₹150 an hour. Clean, easy to reach and with enough parking.
b: Budget play, Half-hour slots, Gear and gutting

ad: Vadrapalya 2nd Block, 72/2, Kothnur, Royal County, 8th Phase, JP Nagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560083
d: Indoor temperature-controlled pool with Nisha Millet coaching across beginner, intermediate and advanced levels including weekend classes, alongside badminton, box cricket, football, basketball and cricket nets. Priced below comparable academies in JP Nagar. Coach turnover has affected consistency, and sessions can be thinly staffed.

ad: Bettadasanapura Bypass Rd, Bettadasanapura Post, Electronic City, S Bingipura, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560105
d: A 25m pool at around ₹200 an hour with a separate kids pool, plus badminton, box cricket, table tennis, a restaurant and on-site stay — day packages bundle the lot, which makes it work as a group outing rather than a booking. Nylon shorts and cap compulsory. Changing rooms are curtained only, and the approach road is rough.

ad: 25/1A, 1st Cross Rd, near Wipro Office, Halanayakanahalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560035
d: Badminton and table tennis alongside boxing, martial arts and a well-equipped gym, with a national-level TT coach and shoe rental at ₹150 for two hours. Sports shop on site. Fees sit above the local average, construction is ongoing, and one reviewer asks management to better regulate walk-in crowding.

ad: Go Krishnappa Layout, Over Tank Road, near Bloomers School, Channasandra, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560067
d: Spacious box cricket turf with bright, even floodlighting and no dark spots — better value than most turfs in the area, and playable in rain. Badminton alongside. Drinking water refills and staff conduct draw repeated complaints, and shuttle visibility dips against the high lighting.

ad: Sy. No. 13, 3rd Cross Rd, Vittal Nagar, Banashankari 5th Stage, Subramanyapura, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560111
d: Four wooden courts under synthetic, ₹150 daytime and ₹200 evenings, with rackets and shuttles on rent and coaching for anyone wanting to build technique. Ample parking outside. Badminton shoes or bare feet only. The strip between the court line and the wall is narrow with people walking through it.

ad: 100 Feet Road, Sarjapura, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560035
d: Five clean, well-maintained courts with racket and shoe rental and plenty of parking, booked through Playo. Ventilation is the problem: it turns into a hot box from about 9 AM to 6 PM on a sunny day, so morning and evening slots are the ones worth taking.

ad: XMPP+GQG, Mahadevapura, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560048
d: Eight standard synthetic courts with notably good lighting and generous parking, next door to SportzHive. Tricky to find the first time. No power backup, though the owner has refunded bookings cut short by outages.

ad: Sy. No. 51/1/17, Doddathogur, Bettadasanapura Main Rd, opposite Passion Elite-I Apartment, Electronic City Phase I, Karnataka 560100
d: Seven courts on professional-grade flooring with certified coaches and a management team that handles scoring and umpiring for corporate tournaments. Parking for two and four wheelers. The access road off the main road is unmade. Reviews on coaching quality are mixed — take a trial before enrolling.

ad: B Hosahalli Road Gate, Varthur–Sarjapur Rd, Sree Narayana Nagar, Chikkadunnasandra, Sompura, Bengaluru, Karnataka 562125
d: Coaching-first academy where the head coach is unusually patient with absolute beginners — parents credit it with keeping a child in the sport long enough to progress to advanced batches. The venue also hosts district-level competitions across other disciplines. Court-allocation disputes have been reported at the desk.

ad: Bhavani Shankara Temple Street, 6th Cross, Srigandhada Kaval, Nagarbhavi 2nd Stage, Arunachalam Layout, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560072
d: Two courts with high-quality synthetic over wooden flooring and good cushioning, very clean toilets, changing rooms and reasonable pricing. Two-wheeler parking only. The court fills almost the whole hall, so there is minimal space to sit or leave your things, and the wall paint makes shuttle tracking harder.
b: Budget play, Small groups, Clean facilities

ad: Suhas Mansion, 39, 2nd Cross, Nagadevanahalli, opposite Government School, Doddagollarahatti, Sir M Vishveshwaraiah Layout, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560110
d: Four wooden courts with synthetic red mats to international lining standards — players report no knee or ankle soreness after long continuous sessions. Spacious, with covered ventilation keeping the heat down, changing rooms and separate washrooms. The location is secluded and feels unsafe at night. Courts 2 and 3 are the ones to book.
b: Long sessions, Coaching, Kids and adults

ad: East, Kasavanahalli, Owners Court Layout, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560035
d: Newer wooden courts open until 1 AM — the latest closing time on this list — with good ventilation, plenty of parking for both two and four wheelers, and coaching focused on technique, footwork and match strategy. Shuttles and rentals are priced well above market, so bring your own.

ad: 494, Muthsandra Main Rd, Varthur, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560087
d: Big, well-kept campus covering swimming, badminton, table tennis, pickleball, football, box cricket, pool and PlayStation, with a food court and proper parking. Swim coaching for young children is the standout — several parents report four and five-year-olds swimming a full length within weeks. A genuine drive out of the city, which is reflected in the pricing.
b: Swimming coaching, Families, Day out, Multi-sport

ad: 1/1, Seegehalli, Aavalahalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560036
d: New wooden courts kept genuinely clean, with high-standard lighting that covers the full court evenly, kids and adult coaching, and plenty of open parking. The owner is hands-on and responsive. The area immediately outside the court is an active construction site, so keep children close.

ad: 211, 14th Cross Rd, 2nd Block, Vishwapriya Nagar, Begur, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560114
d: Four indoor wooden badminton courts with good lighting plus an outdoor turf for box cricket and football, with separate changing rooms for men and women. Newer venue and tidy so far, with coaches reviewers name for beginner kids. Courts are on the small side and parking is two-wheeler only.

ad: Srinivas Garden, 18, 1st Cross, RMV 2nd Stage, Ramakrishnappa Layout, Nagashetty Halli, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560094
d: Four courts arranged in two parallel pairs at around ₹250 an hour, with rackets and shoes on rent at reasonable rates and a friendly owner. Well maintained. No four-wheeler parking, ventilation is poor enough to feel it, and the water dispenser is often not cold.
b: Regular players, Gear rental, Small groups

ad: 21/1, Kempanahalli Village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Yelahanka, Kempanahalli, Karnataka 560064
d: Friendly, community-run court with two named coaches who play with members rather than just instructing, and a regular crowd that makes it easy to join a game solo. Well maintained and usually available without booking far ahead.

raw: Uttarahalli Hobli / Jayanagar Housing Society Layout
ad: P-34, near Maha Prathyangira Temple, Jayanagar Housing Society Layout, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560061
d: New synthetic courts with good grip and knee protection at around ₹200 an hour, with well-regarded coaching in both badminton and table tennis — the hall converts to TT tables on demand. Well maintained and positively reviewed across 541 entries. The location is genuinely remote, so allow travel time.

ad: 34/1, 14th Cross Rd, Ittamadu, Banashankari 3rd Stage, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560085
d: Three well-kept wooden badminton courts plus an outdoor box cricket ground, in a prime Banashankari location with parking, first aid and drinking water. Non-marking shoes are not compulsory. Court 1 catches glare through the door — ask for another if the shuttle is hard to track.

ad: 2nd Floor, Whitefield–Hoskote Rd, behind Golden Car Spa, opposite Royal Convention Hall, Sannatammanahalli, Katamnallur, Karnataka 560049
d: Large playing area covering badminton and table tennis with coaching, a clean lounge and washrooms and ample parking — it hosts TT tournaments. No snacks or juice on site, so bring your own. One reviewer reports being cleared off a court fifteen minutes early over a disputed start time.

ad: 17, off Horamavu Agara Road, Arkavathy Layout, Hennur Gardens, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560113
d: Six to seven courts that are usually available at short notice, with ample parking in a quiet area and dedicated kids’ coaching batches. Two things to know: the roof leaks onto several courts in rain, which has caused at least one slip injury, and the court edges have humps. Shuttles are not included and rental rackets are old.

ad: Seegehalli, 13/3, Basavanapura Rd, Basavanapura, Krishnarajapuram, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560049
d: Good courts on the fourth floor of a school building with friendly staff and a lively atmosphere, plus table tennis. Evenings only. The Playo listing advertises shoe and racket rental that is not actually available on site, so bring your own gear. Not the easiest venue to find first time.
b: Evening play, Table tennis, Own-gear players

ad: Chamundi Hotel Compound, Jayamahal Main Rd, opposite Jayamahal Palace, Jayamahal, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560006
d: Four 7-a-side football courts in the middle of the city, open round the clock, with clean toilets, ample parking and food stalls on site — and one of the only venues in Bengaluru where rugby and ultimate frisbee are played. Parents should note the driveway runs right past the pitch entrance and stray dogs are a recurring problem on the premises.
b: Football, Rugby, Ultimate frisbee, Central location

ad: 3rd Cross Rd, Kodigehalli Main Rd, Shakti Layout, Sadaramangala, Krishnarajapuram, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560067
d: Newly built hybrid courts — wood with a synthetic top — giving good grip and shock absorption, with clear markings and a professional net setup. A proper spectator lobby with spare chairs makes it workable for tournaments. Coaching is well priced. The lights sit a little low and can make the shuttle hard to track.

ad: 11th and 12th Cross, Devasandra Main Rd, Gayathri Layout, Chikkabasavanapura, Krishnarajapuram, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560036
d: Swimming, badminton, billiards, a well-equipped gym and dance classes on one site, with a cafe and a party hall. Swim coaching is the strength — beginners report learning freestyle inside a dozen classes. Non-marking shoes compulsory for badminton. Front-desk conduct draws repeated complaints from parents.

ad: Nanjappa–Thindlu Rd, above Vikas Steel, GD Layout, Doddabommasandra, Vidyaranyapura, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560097
d: 4.9 across 31 reviews. Clean, even turf for box cricket, football and volleyball with lighting built for night matches, a bathroom and a separate area for bags. You can play your own music. Straightforward booking and cooperative staff, at a price reviewers rate as fair.
b: Box cricket, Football, Night games, Groups

ad: Agara Park Gate 1, Service Road
d: Wide paved promenade the whole way round the lake, close to three kilometres and flat throughout. The best-surfaced lake circuit in the city, but there is no water point, one toilet and very little tree cover, so run it early. Gates shut at 10 AM.
after: Plenty of options on the HSR side

n: Agara Lake watch tower and back
ad: Agara Park Gate 4, Sarjapur Main Road
d: Short walk from the Sarjapur Main Road gate along the north bank to the watch tower and back, about 1.6 km. Best in the last hour before the gates shut, with the sunset sitting over the water.

ad: Ulsoor Lake entry gate, opp Hermit Colony
d: Three kilometres of shaded track along the lake, run as an out and back rather than a clean circuit. Toilets on site and water if you ask the gate staff. Gates shut at 10 AM, which lines up with Kaara By The Lake opening at nine for a post-run iced tea.
after: Kaara By The Lake, opens 9 AM

ad: Sankey Tank main entrance, Kodandarampura
d: Wide paved path from the main gate along the water towards the Malleshwaram side, roughly 1.7 km there and back. The track does not close into a full circle, so walkers turn at the far end. Yoga areas and a public gym sit along the way.
t: 5-10 AM, 4-8 PM (Daily) · Early morning or evening

n: Sankey Tank and Malleshwara Park double circuit
ad: Sankey Tank main entrance, Kodandarampura
d: The Sankey shoreline path plus a five-minute walk across to Malleshwara Public Park, which stays open when the tank closes at ten. Clean walkways, a corner exercise station and benches at the far end.
t: Sankey 5-10 AM, 4-8 PM; Malleshwara Park 5 AM-10 PM · Early morning

ad: Sankey Tank main entrance, Kodandarampura
d: Shoreline path at the tank, then up into Sadashivanagara Park for the bamboo walking bay and the pull-up and parallel bars. About 2.8 km end to end, quiet at dawn.
t: Sankey 5-10 AM, 4-8 PM; Sadashivanagara Park 6-10 AM, 4-8 PM · Early morning

n: Agara Lake to HSR Friends Park
ad: Agara Park Gate 1, Service Road
d: Walk out of the Gate 1 side and through the HSR grid to Friends Park, about 1.5 km, where free gym equipment, a yoga space and courts sit on one ground. A sensible add-on when the lake gates shut at ten.
t: Agara 6-10 AM, 4-7 PM; Friends Park 6 AM-7:30 PM · Morning

ad: Agara Park Gate 1, Service Road
d: The same three-kilometre promenade, ridden gently. Cyclists share it with walkers, so it works before seven and not at all in the evening crush. A confidence loop for children and new riders rather than a training ride.
after: Plenty of options on the HSR side

ad: Ulsoor Lake entry gate, opp Hermit Colony
d: Roughly four and a half kilometres from the lake gate into Cubbon Park, through Halasuru and down towards Queens Road before the traffic wakes. Pairs with the car-free Cubbon loop on weekend mornings.
t: Best before 7 AM · Pre-dawn to 7 AM

n: Sankey Tank to Cubbon Park via Race Course Road
ad: Sankey Tank main entrance, Kodandarampura
d: About six kilometres down from the tank onto the green cycling lanes along Race Course Road and into Cubbon Park. Tree cover for most of the second half, and the best stretch of dedicated cycling infrastructure in the city.
t: Best before 7 AM · Pre-dawn to 7 AM

ad: Sankey Tank main entrance, Kodandarampura
d: Lake to lake across the centre of the city, around eight kilometres, picking up the Race Course Road lanes in the middle. A tidy Sunday morning ride with a walk at either end while the gates are open.

ad: Sankey Tank main entrance, Kodandarampura
d: Sankey to Ulsoor to Agara in one go, around twenty kilometres north-west to south-east across the city. A Sunday ride, timed so the gates are open at each stop for a walk and a coffee before the traffic builds.
t: Sunday, before 7 AM · Sunday, pre-dawn start

ad: Lalbagh West Gate, RV Road
d: The four-kilometre circuit with more route variation than anywhere else in the city, and enough of it to keep a long run interesting. Water points and toilets on site, good tree cover, and it stays open into the evening, so you can start late. MTR and Bengaluru Cafe are a short walk out for a post-run dosa.
p: Long runs, Route variation, All-day access
t: Open to about 7:30 PM · Any time; evening runs possible
after: MTR on Lalbagh Road and Bengaluru Cafe nearby

ad: Cubbon Park, Queens Road end
d: Weekends are the point, when the internal roads shut to traffic and you can link a circuit of up to six kilometres. Mornings are as good as running in this city gets. Evenings turn chaotic at the entry gates, so go early or go at the weekend.
p: Long runs, Weekend car-free roads, Group runs
t: Open to about 7 PM; roads closed to cars at weekends · Weekend mornings
after: MG Road and Church Street cafes

ad: Vibhutipura Lake, LBS Nagar
d: Decent paved track around the lake, roughly 2.5 km for the full perimeter, which means a lot of laps for any real distance. No toilets and no water. Cattle wander the path, so watch your footing. Shaded and quiet, and shut by ten.

ad: Doddanekundi Lake
d: A hardened mud track that was one of the best surfaces in east Bengaluru to run on, with outdoor gym equipment and serious birdlife around it. About 60 per cent of it is currently closed for construction work. Worth checking back in six to eight months.
t: Reported open late; confirm before a night run · Hold until the work finishes

ad: Embassy Golf Links Business Park
d: Three and a half kilometres of smooth, unbroken road inside the business park, flat and free of potholes, which makes it the pick locally for tempo work and fast pace. Cars are the limiting factor, so it runs best late in the evening once the campus empties.
p: Tempo runs, Fast pace, Late-night running
t: Late evening is quietest for traffic · Late evening

d: Flat ~4 km paved loop through central Bengaluru's oldest park. Popular Saturday morning meetup for Cubbon Runs.
t: Open daily; group runs Sat 6:00 AM

d: Large Chamrajpet park with shaded walking paths, two or three open-air gyms and a big children's play area with dinosaur statues. There is a lake inside, though a sewage smell drifts in at times. Split hours, shut through the middle of the day.
Small, quiet park on the Air Force HQTC campus at Armane Nagar, used mainly by defence families. Shaded and calm, with little in the way of facilities. Thinly reviewed.
Small shaded park loop — short enough per round that laps stack easily. Quiet before 7 AM.
Wide-footpath road run before traffic builds, with coffee stops at the far end.

n: Indiranagar to Old Airport Road morning loop
d: Short flat city loop via Old Airport Road and Domlur flyover. Common warm-up for riders heading further east.
Quiet residential grid that strings into a flat, well-lit loop before traffic starts. Easy to shorten or extend.
The neighbourhood spine — wide and straight enough to use as a tempo stretch. Quiet before 6:30 AM.

n: HSR to Sarjapur Road morning ride
d: Easy eastbound out-and-back along Sarjapur Road with the option to extend past Dommasandra. Standard weekday spin for the HSR riding crowd.

n: AECS Layout D Block Football Ground — walking and jogging loop
d: Roughly 200-metre perimeter used for walking and jogging around the footballers and cricketers in the middle. Clean and safe for early-morning and late-evening loops, though gates are often shut outside posted hours.
t: Opens around 4:00 PM; check gate notice

d: Heavily shaded park with marked walking paths, outdoor gym equipment, over fifty benches and a kids play area. Dog friendly and well used for jogging and light exercise. Opens at 5 AM.

n: Indian Athletic Academy — Kittur Rani Chennamma Stadium
d: Structured athletics coaching on the stadium track — sprint and distance work, form, and mental preparation, individually tailored. 4.5 across 207 reviews. Coaches take athletes to competition.

BBMP stadium with a well-maintained public running track, open mornings and evenings on clean, spacious grounds. Popular with athletes and casual joggers alike. Washroom hygiene is the recurring complaint.

Lake park developed about two years ago, with a 2.2 km mud running and walking track, an open-air gym and peacocks about. Still being built out. Walkers advise against going alone in the very early morning.

Natural walking track around Attur Lake, close to three kilometres, with an open-air gym, badminton courts and sunrise and sunset views. Recent sewage pollution has hit water quality and the lake ecosystem. Adjacent to the BBMP lake park.

Small scenic lake with a jogging track, walking path, temple, children's play zone and open-air gym. Fresh air, and an easy morning or evening walk. Recent visitors mention rubbish building up in the lake, the smell that follows, and stray dogs around the track.
Central Bengaluru's biggest running track, used by athletes for sprints, long runs and drills. Also hosts Bengaluru FC football matches and other events. Closed Sundays.

Bengaluru's most iconic urban park: a vast tree canopy, running and walking loops, calm mornings and weekend flower shows. Central, and well kept by the horticulture department. The anchor point for running in central Bengaluru, and one of the most reviewed places in the city. Closed Mondays.

Historic Malleshwaram lake dating to 1882, circled by a scenic walking trail of about 1.5 km. Yoga areas, a public gym, children's play space, gazebos and benches. Cyclists are not permitted. Two open sessions daily, and a canonical Bengaluru walking spot.
About 3.5 km of shaded track around the lake; pelicans and wetland birds. Separate joggers' entry on the south-east side.
t: Open daily; joggers' gate opens early morning

d: About a 5 km loop with a mix of paved and mud track; one gate only, so plan the lap.
Dedicated cycle track along Major Sandeep Unnikrishnan Road; lit, with benches.
Park on 17th E Main with an inclined jogging track good for sprint work, plus a gymnastics area. No pets.

n: SAI NCOE Athletics Track — Gnana Bharathi
d: Sports Authority of India synthetic athletics track on the Bengaluru University campus, with hockey, swimming and shooting alongside. Entry needs permission.
Roughly 1 km mud track around Hoodi Lake — unpaved and uneven, but a genuine running loop with cool breezes and few distractions. Avoid after 6 PM, no lighting.

n: ITI Ground & Indoor Sports Facility — Duravani Nagar
d: Large public grass ground open for running and walking, with a basketball court and shade trees. Waterlogs after heavy rain.
Large open ground on Inner Circle Road with a perimeter walking path, kids' park and space for several games at once. Open 24 hours.

Long dirt track running the full shoreline — roughly 4 km of maintained trail, quiet, with pelicans and open sky. One of the best distance loops in north Bengaluru. Not step-free; the track is unpaved.
Small lake with a paved, well-fenced walking track set back from the main road. Clean and guarded, with a children's playground and a lot of waterbirds. Good short loop rather than a distance run.
Roughly 1.25 km gravel walkway around the lake, with outdoor gym, gazebos and a children's play area. Strong birdlife — pelicans, herons, cormorants. Water levels drop in dry months.

South Bengaluru's mountain biking hub, a eucalyptus forest laced with technical off-road trails, 15 to 20 km from Jayanagar. Popular for weekend group rides, with trails from beginner-friendly to technical singletrack. Best in dry weather, as the monsoon turns them to slush.

North Bengaluru's mixed-use township, residential precinct plus retail, laid out with generous greenery, ponds and wide boulevards. Excellent for a quiet, safe, canopy-covered ride without leaving the city. Neither a forest like Cubbon nor a highway route, and a good option for beginners nervous about traffic.

n: Race Course Rd + Bhavan Rd Cycling Lanes
d: Central Bengaluru's dedicated cycling infrastructure: green lanes running along Race Course Road and Bhavan Road and connecting to Cubbon Park. Tree-canopied the whole way, and one of the best urban cycling stretches in the city. Good for a short casual ride, or as a warm-up to a Cubbon Park loop.

Public running track at Kanteerava Stadium, 400 m synthetic when open. Best for speed work and intervals. A ticket is required and access is restricted during events, so check the public timings ahead.

~5-8km rolling trails around Bannerghatta Biological Park area (parts outside the paid zone). Cooler, forested, quieter. Weekend group runs occasionally organised. Watch for early-morning traffic on main road.

Bengaluru's last remaining urban forest, 600 acres of it. Trail running with some steep sections, and popular with mountain bikers and hikers too. Enter by 7 AM, as the sun heats the trail fast. No fee.
~1km walking/jogging path around restored Puttenahalli Lake. Small but scenic. Popular with JP Nagar community. Multiple loops for distance. Restoration led by PNLIT.
A 42 km loop on NICE Road, ridden before 6:30 AM. Well paved, minimal traffic, some elevation, and a popular Sunday spin. After 6:30 the traffic builds and it stops being safe.
src: Bangalore cycling community, Yulu Cycling Meetups

d: Casual 3-4 km loop inside Cubbon Park (on car-free Saturdays and Sundays). Perfect for beginners, kids, urban commuters, gentle spin. No traffic on weekends.

Shaded walking paths winding between the granite outcrops off Bull Temple Road, with an open-air gym area. Roughly a 15-minute loop back to the Bull Temple Road gate. Litter around the rocks is the recurring complaint.
Big tree-covered park with a proper running track, three gates and a basketball court alongside. A full circuit takes 20 to 25 minutes at walking pace. Free entry and recently well maintained.
Small triangular park on Bull Temple Road with an open gym inside and a short walking circuit. Locals also use it for casual badminton. Restricted gate timings.
Neighbourhood park off 16th Cross with clean walkways, a corner exercise station and plenty of benches. Planting is patchy but the paths are kept up.
Wide walking bay under bamboo groves just off Sankey Tank, with pull-up and parallel bars for calisthenics. Quiet at dawn and popular with early walkers.
Short lakeside stroll beside Sankey Tank with sunset views and a calm, low-traffic path. Free entry, parking outside. Lighting is thin after dark.
Large park off South End Road with old trees, two children's areas and an open gym, though the equipment is worn. Central, busy and easy to reach from Jayanagar or Hombegowda Nagar.
Level walking track with tactile paving running the perimeter, stone pergolas every 200 m, plus yoga and outdoor gym space. Diagonally across from Jayanagar metro, open around the clock.
Long rectangular park on 80 Feet Road opposite Wipro, dense enough with trees to feel like a pocket forest. Paved paths and benches. Mosquitoes are bad in the evening and traffic noise carries.
Small 6th Block park with a walking track, basic outdoor gym and a kids' play area. Evening-only on most days — gates open from 4:30 PM.
Sector 3 park that works as a full outdoor fitness stop — walking paths, free gym equipment, yoga space, plus football, volleyball and badminton on the same ground.
Sector 1 park behind Assetz 27 Park Avenue with a well-designed walking path, gazebo, open-air theatre seating and an outdoor gym. Quiet and full of birdsong; the gym equipment rusts in the open.
Compact Sector 2 park with heavy shade that makes daytime running bearable, an amphitheatre that hosts events and an open gym. Carry repellent for evenings.
Green Sector 4 park with a walking track and kids' area, and one of the few nearby that stays open through the afternoon. Roadside parking is easy.
East along CMH Road from the 12th Main junction toward Old Madras Rd. Heavy heat on the heatmap; wide footpath but busy traffic. Best before 7 AM.
South along 80 Feet Road from 12th Main to the Domlur flyover. One of the darkest corridors in the Indiranagar heatmap. Signal-interrupted.
Short connector from 12th Main west to Double Road Park. Feeds the Defence Colony grid loops.
Rectangular loop through the Defence Colony inner roads north of CMH Road. Low traffic, tree cover, popular for repeats.
East along Thippasandra Main Rd through HAL 3rd Stage. Connects Kuvempu Park and GP Raja Ratnam Park; commercial stretch, busier after 8 AM.

n: Wheeler Road Extension — north to south
d: Straight north-south run down Wheeler Road Extension through Cooke Town. The main street route in an area with almost no park options.
Northbound along Jayamahal Main Road past the palace grounds. Wide shoulder, long uninterrupted stretch.

n: Bellandur Lake Road — south to north
d: North along Bellandur Lake Road from the ORR side. Dark heat on the Strava layer despite the lake itself being unusable — runners use the road, not the water's edge.

n: Kadubeesanahalli Road — APH to IPRR junction
d: Uphill stretch from Ambalipura Halli Road to the Inner Peripheral Ring Road junction. Short, steep, used for repeats.
Grid loop through the industrial layout roads north of Doddanekkundi Lake. Very low traffic before 7 AM; the densest heat cluster in the Mahadevapura tile.
Long west-bound stretch of Whitefield Road. Continuous footpath most of the way; heavy traffic after 7:30 AM.

n: Pattandur Agrahara Metro to Kadugodi Tree Park Metro
d: Metro-to-metro run along the Whitefield main road. Useful point-to-point — start at one station, finish at the other.
Loop around the ITI grounds and adjacent roads. Grass ground in the middle, road perimeter; waterlogs after heavy rain.
Out-and-back along Sankey Road from the tank to the Palace Ground side. Dark heat; the classic Malleshwaram street run.
Runs the road parallel to the Palace Grounds boundary. Long uninterrupted stretch, wide shoulder, one of the few road options in a tight area.
Northbound past the palace grounds. Duplicate anchor to RT-060 but filed to Vasanth Nagar, which has almost no road options.
Wide arterial with continuous footpath. Heavily used early; commercial and busy after 8 AM.
Short sustained climb toward Nandi Durga Road. Used for hill repeats — the only gradient in the tile.
East from Vidyapeetha Circle toward the Outer Ring Road. Wide, straight, moderate heat.
Short steep repeat stretch on the BDA layout roads. The main gradient option in south-west Bengaluru.

Roughly 1.2 km paved loop around the lake, tree-covered for most of the way, with an active walkers association. Strong birdlife including peacocks on the island. Water level drops and smells in dry months.

Fully paved loop around the lake with a children's play area, benches and public toilet. Stroller-friendly, dust-free and quiet — one of the better-kept lakes in the eastern corridor. Back section is less maintained.

n: Kowdenahalli Lake And Park — Dr Ambedkar Nagar
d: 1.4 km fenced loop on a mud track — easier on the joints than paved surfaces. Wide enough for two-way traffic, with a children's play area. Water quality is inconsistent and smells in places.

Roughly 4.5 km circuit — one of the longest lake loops in the city, rejuvenated and heavy with birdlife including migratory species. The trail does not quite close at one end, and a storm-water drain smells on part of the stretch.
Large community park with a long walking path, open gym in working order, seating decks throughout and a kids' play area. Gets crowded and dusty at peak times.
Recently renovated with a widened walking track, gym equipment at three points, sheltered seating and clean washrooms. Bright lighting makes it usable late. No kids' play area.
Open 24 hours — rare for a BBMP park. Good walking paths, open gym, children's area and a laughing club in the mornings. Cricket often in progress on one side.
Small neighbourhood park on 7th Main with a short walking circuit and kids' play equipment. Mornings only. Dusty from the main road.

A 2.15 km track around the lake behind the Bellandur tech blocks — known locally as a birding spot, best around 6:45 AM and peak season November to March. Clean, uncrowded, no mosquitoes. Water levels drop sharply outside the rains.

Roughly 4 km around the lake — a long stretch for walking and running, with benches on the cliff side for sunset. The north side is well kept; the south side has poor fencing and a mushy path. No lighting after dark.
t: Daily, morning and evening; one gate only

n: Vijaya Bank Layout Main Park — Vijaya Bank Layout
d: Long walking circuit suited to distance, with a separate seniors' gym, kids' play area, toilets and heavy tree cover. Busy at peak hours — quiet mid-morning.

Bengaluru's only accessible forest hill — trail running and hiking on rocky tracks with multiple viewpoints, peacocks and genuine quiet. Two ways up: a sharp direct ascent or a longer loop around the base. ₹10 entry, cash only. Gate opens 5:30 AM.

About 1.6 km round on a lit track managed by the forest department — usable before dawn, with an island in the middle that draws birdwatchers. One stretch stinks and half the lake dries out in low-rain years.
Nine acres with a long jogging circuit, stone sculptures along the path, an open mini-auditorium and a kids' play area. Roomy enough that it rarely feels crowded. Pets no longer allowed.

A 1.1 km rectangular circuit through dense tree cover — closer to a mini forest than a park, with criss-cross paths that extend it to about 2 km. Mud walkway, open gym, signage on local flora. Small entry fee.
Paved walkway right around the lake, about 1.8 km a full round. Heavy birdlife — peacocks, kingfishers, barbets, herons. Part of the lake dries out and one stretch carries a drainage smell.

n: Ramaiah City Park — MS Ramaiah City Layout
d: Walking track through well-kept greenery with a large open lawn, mud play area and two landscaped mounds. Set back from the main road so it stays quiet. Limited opening hours.

Wide clean paths inside, but the real draw is the gated streets around it — a genuinely good early-morning running circuit, usable from 4 AM to 11 PM. Skate ring and a meditation space on site. Inner walkways are narrow.
t: Daily 6:00 AM – 9:00 PM; surrounding roads always open

n: Dr. B R Ambedkar Stadium — Rajajinagar Industrial Town
d: Public stadium with a proper athletics track alongside walking paths, basketball and badminton courts, a skating rink, cricket pitch and mini gym. Coaching available. Busy all day; parking is difficult.
t: Open daily, dawn to late evening

d: Spacious public stadium used for running events and general sport. Open to the public on a timetable — locked outside those hours, which reviewers complain about at weekends.
The biggest park in this pocket — a 600–700 m perimeter circuit under heavy tree cover, with a BBMP library, meditation centre, public gym and kids' area. Multiple entrances, guarded.

n: Mahatma Gandhi BDA Park — Nagarbhavi 2nd Stage
d: The largest of several parks in this pocket, with a walking path, statues, open gym and kids' area under dense tree cover. The path surface is uneven — poor for fast running, fine for walking.

A 1.38 km walking and running loop around a historic 47-acre lake, shaded by old trees on both sides so it reads more like a forest path than a city park. Open gym, kids' zone and yoga spot. Drainage inflow smells in places; watch for street dogs at the entrance.
